 Flyers @ Senators: How to watch, lineups, and gamethread
 The Flyers look to rebound against the visiting Sabres in their home stand finale.
 Posted on November 19, 2026 November 19, 2026 by Thomas Williams 
 Photo credit: Heather Barry 
 The Philadelphia Flyers have an opportunity to build off of their solid performance against the Buffalo Sabres with a visit up to Canada’s capital. The Ottawa Senators will pose a big threat, but they’ve been here before.
 Puck drop:  7:00 p.m.
 How to watch/listen: 
📺: NBCSP
📻: 97.5 The Fanatic
 Pregame reading
 The Flyers need to find a way to consistently get their own scoring chances. Offense has been hard to come by for this team, but they are inching closer towards being able to sustain a certain level. [BSH] 
 Danny Briere had to go on local radio and dispel the recent Cutter Gauthier-related report that there was some promise from Chuck Fletcher that was then not kept by the current regime. [BSH] 
 Speaking of rumors, Elliotte Friedman recently said that because of some recent reports surrounding Travis Konecny, it’s clear someone in the Flyers organization has an agenda against him, and is telling a certain reporter all about how much he shouldn’t be a part of this team for much longer. [BSH]

 Storylines to watch
 Powering through an elite defense 
 While it doesn’t seem like they are on-paper, the Senators are one of the best defensive teams in hockey right now. They are allowing just 1.88 goals against per 60 at 5-on-5, which is the second-fewest in the league — only the Minnesota Wild are better. Additionally, they’re allowing the fourth-fewest expected goals per 60 at 5-on-5, as well. It’s just a really good, shutdown hockey team over there that can be coached to winning a whole lot of hockey games.
 The Flyers are going to have to push through that tall task and hopefully chip away at it. They are getting much better at putting shots on the board over the past week and a bit, but will it be enough to potentially get enough goals to secure a win over this solid Ottawa team?
 Can Owen Tippett get going? 
 A major problem for the Flyers has been the lack of production from some mid-20s veterans and Owen Tippett is at the center of it all. He has just six points in 18 games played — a far cry from his 28-goal, 51-point performance he put in last season. But he did get on the board against the Sabres and looked slightly more effective. So, can he then have that be a jumping off point?
 The Flyers desperately need him to step up if they want to win some hockey games. While having Matvei Michkov go nuts in his third year in the league and prove that he can be the best player on this team, having a supporting cast beyond him is just as crucial and Tippett could be here for a long time if he can keep on doing that. But now, there are questions being raised if he can even be a regular 50-point guy.
 Multiple goaltending storylines 
 For the Flyers, they are returning to Joseph Woll for this one after he earned the win over the Sabres. It’s a solid call, to just keep with the hot hand, but after a season where Rick Tocchet has largely done a simple rotation, it’s something notable. It only becomes a real story if we’re seeing a true starter-backup deployment between Woll and Dan Vladar over the next couple of weeks, but for now it’s something that just makes you go “hmm”.
 Over there on the Senators, Sam Ersson will be in between the pipes. Our dear, old friend Sam Ersson. Selfishly, it’s a massive opportunity to take advantage of one of the worst goalies in the league and now the Flyers forwards could really get some scoring in (hopefully) but it would also be so Flyers if Ersson suddenly gets a shutout against his former team. Even a win for him would be massive.
